intro: Permission and prohibition with nuance: conditions, limits, and standing up to a ban.
p.autorización.consejo: It is feminine and ends in -ción: «una autorización». It comes from «autorizar», which is spelled with z.
p.autorizar.consejo: The z is written before a, o, u: «autorizo». Before e it changes to c: «autorice».
p.te parecería bien que.glosa: would you be fine with it if…
p.te parecería bien que.consejo: It takes the imperfect subjunctive: «¿te parecería bien que fuera?». With «usted»: «¿le parecería bien…?».
p.sería posible.consejo: An infinitive follows: «¿sería posible salir antes?». With «sería» the request sounds softer than with «es».
p.dar permiso para.consejo: After «para» comes an infinitive: «¿me das permiso para salir?». Permission is asked for and given.
p.siempre y cuando.consejo: It works like «siempre que» and also takes the subjunctive: «siempre y cuando vuelvas».
p.solo si.consejo: It takes the indicative: «solo si vuelves». «Solo» no longer needs an accent, even when it means «únicamente».
p.salvo que.consejo: It asks for the subjunctive: «salvo que llueva». You also say «excepto que» or «a menos que».
p.que sea la última vez.glosa: let it be the last time
p.que sea la última vez.consejo: The «que» at the start expresses a wish or a soft order: «que sea la última vez».
p.te prohíbo que.consejo: It has an accent on the í: «prohíbo». It takes the subjunctive: «te prohíbo que salgas».
p.eso no se hace.consejo: It is what you say to children. It does not speak about a specific person: «se hace» is impersonal.
p.de todas formas.consejo: It is the same as «de todos modos». You say it when you do not change your mind: «iré de todas formas».
p.atreverse a.consejo: It is pronominal and takes «a»: «me atrevo a hablar». Its opposite is «no atreverse».
p.contar con.consejo: The o becomes «ue»: «cuento con», «cuentas con». With a pronoun: «cuento contigo».
b1.texto:
**Asking for permission**, from normal to most careful:

- **¿Me das permiso para** salir antes?
- **¿Te parecería bien que** saliera antes?
- **¿Sería posible** salir antes?
- **¿Cuento con tu autorización?**

**Giving it without limits:** **por supuesto**, **cómo no**, **cuando quieras**.

**Giving it with limits.** Watch the mood after each connector:

- **Siempre y cuando vuelvas** antes de las doce. (subjunctive)
- **Solo si vuelves** antes de las doce. (indicative)
- **Salvo que sea** una urgencia. (subjunctive)
- **Que sea la última vez.**

**Forbidding.** **Te prohíbo que** me **hables** así. To a child: **Eso no se hace.**

**Rejecting a ban:** **¿Quién dice que no se puede?** **Lo haré de todas formas.**
b2.f0.texto: Dad, would it be all right with you if I went to the concert on Sergio's motorbike?
b2.f1.texto: I forbid you to get on that motorbike.
b2.f3.texto: You can go by bus, as long as you come back before one.
b2.f4.texto: Would it be possible to come back with Laura's mother?
b2.f5.texto: You can come back with her, unless she leaves very late.
b2.f6.texto: So, do you give me permission to go?
b2.f7.texto: Yes, let it be the last time.
b4.texto:
The mood of the verb depends on the phrase:

- **Siempre y cuando** + subjunctive: **siempre y cuando vuelvas**.
- **Salvo que** + subjunctive: **salvo que sea** una urgencia.
- **Solo si** + indicative: **solo si vuelves**.
- **¿Te parecería bien que…?** + imperfect subjunctive: **¿te parecería bien que saliera?**

To forbid: **te prohíbo que** + subjunctive. With children you say **eso no se hace**.
b4.e0.texto: You can go out only if you come back before twelve.
b4.e1.texto: You cannot come in, unless it is an emergency.
b5.f0.texto: Night falls slowly over the bus stop.
b5.f1.texto: On the wet pavement, the headlights draw yellow circles.
b5.f2.texto: Marta squeezes the ticket in her hand and looks at the empty street.
b5.f3.texto: Her father has written the permission slip in large, tight handwriting.
b5.f4.texto: The bus arrives with a sigh of brakes and opens its doors.
b5.f5.texto: At the back, a group of friends sings a cheerful song.
b5.f6.texto: Marta does not dare to sit with them at first.
b5.f7.texto: A girl makes room for her and smiles at her.
b5.f8.texto: The bus pulls away among red lights and flashes of rain.
b5.f9.texto: Marta rests her forehead on the cold glass and finally breathes, calm.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «siempre y cuando» takes the subjunctive.
b6.o1.refuerzo: That is indicative; here you need the subjunctive.
b6.o2.refuerzo: It is future; after «siempre y cuando» comes the subjunctive.
b6.pregunta: Complete the condition with the right verb.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: it is what you typically say to a child.
b7.pregunta: A child hits another. What do you say?
b8.o0.refuerzo: After «solo si» the present subjunctive is not used.
b8.o2.refuerzo: It would be an unreal hypothesis, not a real condition.
b8.pregunta: Complete the condition with the right verb.
b9.frase: Te prohíbo que me hables así
b9.traduccion: I forbid you to speak to me like that
b10.o0.refuerzo: «Porque» gives a cause, not an exception.
b10.o2.refuerzo: «Aunque» admits a difficulty, not an exception.
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «Would it be possible to leave early?»
b12.o0.refuerzo: It is a sentence for correcting a child.
b12.o1.refuerzo: It does not ask permission: it rejects the ban.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Yes: it politely asks whether you have permission.
b12.pregunta: Which sentence asks for permission formally?
p.papá.consejo: A familiar word for father. The stress is on the last syllable.
p.moto.consejo: Short for «motocicleta». Everyday speech uses the short form.
p.subas.consejo: After «prohibir que» the subjunctive is needed: «que subas».
p.peligrosa.consejo: From «peligro», danger. Its feminine form matches a feminine noun.
p.vuelvas.consejo: «volver» changes o to ue; the subjunctive appears after «que».
p.das.consejo: «das» is a short, one-syllable form of «dar». Note the accent is absent.
p.urgencia.consejo: Starts with «urgente». The g before e sounds like h.
p.acera.consejo: The part of the street where people walk. Its opposite is «calzada», the road.
p.faros.consejo: The lights at the front of a car. Here it appears in the plural.
p.frenos.consejo: From «frenar», to stop. The verb is «frenar».
p.atreve.consejo: From «atreverse», to dare. The v sounds like b.
p.sentarse.consejo: The «se» is part of the verb: it means to sit oneself down.
p.arranca.consejo: For vehicles, «arrancar» means to start moving or start the engine.
p.destellos.consejo: From «destellar», to sparkle. The ll and y sound like «y».
